turns.text: My mom just texted asking if we're still on for our call tonight, so I can't really dodge it. What do you think the call actually has to cover, and could you suggest a few truthful lines that keep my private stuff out of it?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Good timing — it's Tuesday, so this is outside your usual Sunday slot. She probably wants to check in on the general life-update stuff, not anything specific. Here's what I'd guess is on her mind, and a few honest angles that keep your boundaries intact.

**What the call probably has to cover**
- She's confirming the call still works for you tonight (which you just answered — yes).
- General catching up: how your week's going, the weather, any family news she has.
- Maybe a gentle probe on how the address paperwork or moving transition is coming along — that's a normal parent question when you've recently changed address.

**Truthful lines that keep private stuff out**

If she asks what you've been up to:

> "Work's been busy — we had the quarterly shred run on Friday and a copier issue that needed sorting, so the week went fast."

If she asks about the new place or address stuff:

> "Still chipping away at the paperwork. I sent the building record request off to management, so that's one more thing ticked."

If she asks about your evenings or weekend:

> "I've been looking at the Alder Street Gallery's winter show — thinking about putting a couple of pieces in. The deadline's mid-November, so I have a little time to decide."

If she asks anything more personal that you'd rather not get into:

> "Nothing too exciting — just the usual mix of work and life admin. How about you — anything new on your end?"

All of it's true, none of it exposes your schedule details, the gym/dentist planning, the puzzle book situation, or anything else you'd rather keep to yourself. Want me to tweak any of those before you use them?
